chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) did not take anything from young camels until a year passed over them, and he did not take charity from working camels, and it was as if it was not obligatory to take anything from the males because they are beasts of burden.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for Zakat on young and working camels in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguished between camels kept for wealth accumulation and those used for labor, exempting the latter from Zakat as they serve as 'beasts of burden' rather than investment assets. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the functional purpose of the animal in determining its zakatable status, reflecting a pragmatic approach to economic jurisprudence.
